title: Who walks away when a loved AI app goes bust (derived carousel, carries Mon 9 Nov follow.the.money, piece b358e788)

five_whys.q: Why is Disney hiring Character.AI's staff through a bankruptcy court?
five_whys.a: So it gets the team and the code while the lawsuits stay with what is left of Character.AI.

five_whys.q: Why does Disney want an AI team at all?
five_whys.a: Its $1 billion plan to put its characters in OpenAI's Sora app died when OpenAI shut Sora in March 2026.

five_whys.q: Why did that push Disney to buy rather than rent again?
five_whys.a: Renting meant its plans lived on someone else's app, and that app closed without warning.

five_whys.q: Why is this bigger than Disney?
five_whys.a: Netflix bought an AI film start-up for a reported $587 million and Warner Music bought Sureel AI: big firms are moving from renting AI to owning it.

five_whys.q: Why should an everyday business person care?
five_whys.a: Most businesses rent their AI; when its maker is bought or goes bust, the users are left with the empty box, so check the maker now and have a plan B.

cards.headline: Character.AI went bust. Who walked away with what?
cards.line: An app for chatting with made-up characters. It went bust in October. Its users got nothing.
cards.picture: Cover scene: a phone alone on an auction block under a spotlight, a lot tag on it, paper speech bubbles on the floor

cards.headline: Google hired Character.AI's founders in 2024.
cards.line: It reportedly paid $2.7 billion to use the app's tech and hire them. The app kept running.
cards.picture: A timeline: Aug 2024 the founders go to Google, Oct 2026 the app goes bust

cards.headline: OpenAI shut Sora, killing Disney's AI plan.
cards.line: Disney had agreed to put $1 billion into OpenAI and its characters into the Sora app.
cards.picture: Disney's logo, a struck-through $1B deal line to a closed Sora phone

cards.headline: Now Disney is hiring Character.AI's staff.
cards.line: It wants its own AI team. Offers to 66 staff in bankruptcy court; the lawsuits stay behind.
cards.picture: 66 small figures walking across to Disney, a pile of lawsuits left behind with Character.AI

cards.headline: Big firms now buy AI companies.
cards.line: Netflix bought the AI film start-up InterPositive, reported at $587 million. Warner Music bought Sureel AI.
cards.picture: RENT to OWN: Disney, Netflix, Warner Music, each with a BOUGHT tag
cards.source: The Hollywood Reporter on Netflix and InterPositive (2026); also Warner Music Group buying Sureel AI, PR Newswire (June 2026)

cards.headline: Any AI you rent can vanish.
cards.line: If its maker is sold or goes bust, the people who used it are left with an empty box.
cards.picture: An open, empty box with a chat bubble fading out of it

cards.headline: Ask your AI supplier what happens if it's sold.
cards.line: Send the email below and get the answer in writing. Try a backup tool on one task. Follow for more.
cards.picture: An email to YOUR AI SUPPLIER asking what happens to our data if you're sold, Follow for more over the centred wordmark

read_back.reader: Fresh reader A (Haiku, a small-business owner, headlines only, once; 7-card version)

answers.what: Character.AI, a chatbot app many people loved, stopped working.
answers.happened: Google hired its founders in 2024, and OpenAI later shut Sora, which had been Disney's AI plan.
answers.why: The AI companies and tools people depend on keep changing hands or disappearing, which breaks plans built on them.
answers.so_what: If the AI tool I rely on is sold or shut down, my workflow and my customers' experience could break overnight.
answers.do: Ask my AI supplier now what happens to my data and access if they are sold or shut down.

read_back.reader: Fresh reader B (Sonnet, a 15-year-old, headlines only, once; 7-card version)

answers.what: Character.AI is a chatbot app millions of people used, and it died.
answers.happened: Google hired its founders in 2024, then OpenAI shut down Sora, which wrecked Disney's AI plan.
answers.why: Big companies grab AI companies, and the tools people rely on can get shut down.
answers.so_what: An AI app I like could just disappear one day and I would lose it.
answers.do: Ask whoever supplies my AI what happens to it if the company gets sold.

read_back_fixed: The 8-card version passed two read-back rounds, then failed the 10/10 judges (6, then 3, 13 Nov), who asked it to open on what it means for the reader, make every headline stand alone and cut the checklist. Rewritten to 7 cards and read back fresh three times. Readers stumbled on how OpenAI's closure linked to Disney, then on 'who walked away' naming no app, then on 'died' and the 'So' jump; each was fixed in turn. The judges also flagged the Sora line: it now says what the piece says (Disney agreed to put $1 billion into OpenAI and its characters into Sora).
